target_customer: US hospitals and healthcare facilities that pay to hire long term foreign nurses and other clinicians; candidates apply free
problem: Hospitals struggle to staff nurses, and recruiting nurses from abroad is slowed by immigration, licensing and credentialing complexity.
business_model: Placement fee paid by facilities for long term staff; Flint covers candidate immigration and licensing costs (per company site and a directory, unverified)
product_category: International nurse recruitment with immigration and licensing technology

founders.name: Kenton Jarvie
founders.background_notes: YC page describes a blend of business acumen and a liberal arts background; no employers or schools stated.

founders.name: Anson Kung
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page and a YC job post; no biography found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly a services and workflow business with software for credentialing and visa tracking; legal and operational work dominates.

defensibility.rationale: Immigration expertise and hospital relationships help, but large staffing firms such as AMN already recruit international nurses.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Flint. Visa retrogression in 2023 to 2025 delayed foreign nurse arrivals industry wide per Becker's and Bloomberg reporting.

market_need_then: Hospital nurse shortages and a backlog of foreign nurse green cards: the AAIHR estimated at least 10,000 foreign nurses held up by retrogression (2023 reporting, after the batch); no 2020 dated demand source was opened.

branding.domain_note: Uses withflint.com, a prefix domain rather than flint.com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Candidate friendly: your green card pathway starts here

branding.brand_signature: Tagline: Your green card pathway starts here; weekly free webinars hosted for candidates

brand_strength.rationale: No press on the brand found; the word Flint collides with the city and many other companies in search.

outcome_analysis: Flint is active with about 50 people per the YC page and works across 20 or more states per a YC job post. Funding is poorly documented: aggregators show roughly 4 to 5M raised with a seed dated October 2025, none confirmed by a primary source. The business depends on immigration visa availability, which was hit by retrogression delays after the batch. The outcome is unclear.
notes: Funding unverified: Caplight lists a 5M total and an October 2025 seed, another directory 4.12M across three rounds, neither confirmed by press or SEC; not recorded as rounds. A YC job post names Haystack VC and Audacious Ventures as backers with no amounts. Location differs (YC says Vancouver, PitchBook says Menlo Park). Competitor search returned only retrogression news from 2023 onward and nothing dated near the 2020 batch. No complaints or shutdown found; search results were dominated by Flint, Michigan. Completeness pass: rounds recorded from a PitchBook-derived directory (healthcarediscovery.ai: 125K accelerator 2020-08, seed 2021-09 with no amount) and Caplight (seed 2025-10, 5M stated as total raised, round amount unknown). Each rests on a single database; totals conflict (4.12M, 5M, 8M in a recruiter post, a 15M Series A on AngelBacked not recorded) and no press or SEC filing confirms any. Dates may overlap or duplicate.
